excerpt_i18n.en: In recent years, as artificial intelligence has gradually moved out of laboratories and into the real world, the issue of perception has returned to the center of technological discussion. From autonomous driving and smart devices to spatial intelligence and embodied intelligence, systems are no longer just about understanding information but must continuously acquire reliable signals in complex, dynamic physical environments. In practical applications, the limitations of relying solely on visual perception are increasingly exposed, prompting both academia and industry to reconsider the role of multimodal perception in the next generation of intelligent systems. Against this backdrop, wireless sensing technologies such as acoustic waves and millimeter waves are gaining attention. These technologies do not aim to "see" but instead enable devices to understand environments and behaviors by modeling and analyzing physical signals, without adding extra burden or interfering with users. While still far from widespread adoption, they are seen as a crucial foundation for supporting spatial intelligence and real-world interaction. During GAIR 2025, Zhang Jin, an associate professor at Southern University of Science and Technology, shared insights on wireless sensing, multimodal perception, and new sensing technologies for spatial intelligence. With extensive experience in related research, she focuses more on the feasibility and reliability of these technologies in real-world scenarios, rather than just their performance under experimental conditions. At the conference, AI Tech Review engaged in a dialogue with Professor Zhang Jin about wireless sensing and its applications in the real world. In the conversation, rather than offering broad judgments on the technology's prospects, she preferred to discuss the limitations and challenges faced by sensing technologies during implementation, drawing from her research practice, and shared her own remarkable personal experiences.

items.title: Pixlio – Browser-based AI image editing tools
items.raw_excerpt: I'm the builder behind Pixlio. Pixlio is a browser-based AI image editor and generator for common tasks like background replacement and photo effects. I built it because I kept needing repeatable image edits for various cases. I wanted a workflow that doesn't require users to be good at prompt writing, since many tools mostly provide a prompt field. Pixlio is built with Astro and runs on Cloudflare Workers. There's a one-click signup and a small amount of free credits so you can try the core flows quickly. Image processing has real per-request costs, so it can't be unlimited free - paid credits cover heavier usage. I'd love feedback on (1) the editor workflow and (2) what kind of image tools would be most useful next.

items.title: 摩尔线程王华：万卡训练中，最危险的往往是「不报错」｜GAIR 2025
items.raw_excerpt: 作者｜包永刚 编辑｜林觉民 2025年12月12-13日，第八届GAIR全球人工智能与机器人大会在深圳·博林天瑞喜来登酒店正式启幕。 作为AI 产学研投界的标杆盛会，GAIR自2016年创办以来，始终坚守“传承+创新”内核，始终致力于连接技术前沿与产业实践。 在人工智能逐步成为国家竞争核心变量的当下，算力正以前所未有的速度重塑技术路径与产业结构。13日举办的「AI 算力新十年」专场聚焦智能体系的底层核心——算力，从架构演进、生态构建到产业化落地展开系统讨论，试图为未来十年的中国AI产业，厘清关键变量与发展方向。 王华在「AI算力新十年」论坛发表了主题为《基于国产GPU集群的大规模训练实践》的演讲。 当海外头部公司已经建设十万卡、甚至二十万卡规模的 GPU 集群，万卡训练正在从“前沿探索”转变为大模型研发的基础设施能力。模型参数规模进入万亿级之后，真正拉开差距的，已不再只是单卡性能，而是训练周期能否被压缩、系统是否长期稳定、工程效率能否支撑高频迭代。 在这样的背景下，万卡训练所面临的挑战也发生了根本变化。 节点故障、性能抖动、通信与存储瓶颈，在集群规模被放大之后都会成为常态问题，很多在千卡规模下可以容忍的风险，在万卡场景中都会被大幅放大。 王华在演讲中将结合摩尔线程在国产 GPU 万卡级真实集群上的训练实践，系统拆解这一过程中遇到的关键难题，以及相应的工程解法。从并行策略选择、训练前的模拟与起飞检查，到异步 Checkpoint、慢节点治理，再到静默数据错误、Hang 以及 Inf/NaN 等稳定性问题的应对， 他重点分享如何通过软件栈、自动化与可观测体系，把万卡训练从“能跑”推进到“可持续稳定地跑”。 这些经验并非实验室结论，而是来自真实生产环境中反复验证后的工程积累，他希望摩尔线程的经验能够给想要做万卡训练的公司和机构一些借鉴。 以下是王华演讲的精彩内容，雷峰网作了不改变

Author: Bao Yonggang  Editor: Lin Juemin  
On December 12-13, 2025, the 8th GAIR Global Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Summit officially commenced at the Sheraton Shenzhen Boao Tianrui Hotel.  
As a benchmark event in the AI industry-academia-research-investment sector, GAIR has consistently adhered to the core principle of "heritage + innovation" since its inception in 2016, dedicated to bridging cutting-edge technology with industrial practice.  
As artificial intelligence increasingly becomes a core variable in national competition, computing power is reshaping technological pathways and industrial structures at an unprecedented pace. The "AI Computing Power: The Next Decade" session held on the 13th focused on computing power—the foundational core of intelligent systems—engaging in systematic discussions from architectural evolution and ecosystem development to industrial implementation, aiming to clarify key variables and development directions for China's AI industry over the next decade.  
Wang Hua delivered a speech titled "Large-Scale Training Practices Based on Domestic GPU Clusters" at the "AI Computing Power: The Next Decade" forum.  
While leading overseas companies have already established GPU clusters with scales of 100,000 or even 200,000 cards, 10,000-card training is transitioning from "frontier exploration" to a fundamental infrastructure capability for large model development. As model parameters reach the trillion-level, what truly creates a gap is no longer just single-card performance, but whether training cycles can be compressed, systems can remain stable long-term, and engineering efficiency can support high-frequency iteration.  
Against this backdrop, the challenges faced by 10,000-card training have fundamentally shifted.  
Node failures, performance fluctuations, and communication and storage bottlenecks become routine issues as cluster scales expand, with many problems that were manageable at the thousand-card scale now...

En un momento en que la inteligencia artificial se está convirtiendo gradualmente en una variable central en la competencia entre naciones, la potencia de cálculo está remodelando las rutas tecnológicas y las estructuras industriales a una velocidad sin precedentes. La sesión especial "La Nueva Década de la Potencia de Cálculo en IA", celebrada el día 13, se centró en la potencia de cálculo, núcleo fundamental de los sistemas inteligentes, abarcando desde la evolución de la arquitectura y la construcción del ecosistema hasta la producción.
